prompt: tailwind v4 cheatsheet -- just switched from v3, need the new stuff

usability.notes: Excellent organization from basics to advanced with migration content properly sequenced. Outstanding scannability via numbered cards, Tags, and RefRow tables. The 3-column v3→v4 Quick Reference is a standout desk-reference artifact. Visual variety is strong throughout — Code, RefRow, Bullet, KV, and custom metric/strikethrough tables all appear. Information density is well-calibrated; no filler, no walls of text. Minor deductions prevented by borderline thinness in Sections 18 and 21, but overall this is immediately bookmarkable by a working developer.

completeness.notes: Covers all major v4 paradigm shifts a v3 migrator needs: CSS-first config, @theme, @utility, @custom-variant, @plugin, container queries, 3D transforms, gradient overhaul, new variants, dark mode changes, and a concrete migration checklist with the upgrade tool. Useful extras like @reference, @source not, named containers, and oklch context exceed the prompt. Gaps: @config for incremental v3 compatibility deserves its own section (only a bullet tip); CSS variable shorthand in arbitrary values missing; @import 'tailwindcss/utilities' selective import not covered; theme() function behavior change absent; renamed utility list is illustrative rather than comprehensive.

accuracy.notes: All 8 verified claims are accurate against official Tailwind CSS v4 documentation. Installation commands, CSS-first config directives (@import, @theme, @source not, @utility, @custom-variant with @slot), gradient renames (bg-gradient-to-* → bg-linear-to-*), container queries built into core, the upgrade tool (npx @tailwindcss/upgrade), and performance benchmarks (≤10x full, ≤100x incremental) are all confirmed. One minor imprecision: the @screen → @media replacement shows a hardcoded pixel value (width >= 768px) where the idiomatic v4 form would reference the theme token via theme(--breakpoint-md), but this is a copy-paste-safe value and not a breaking error. No hallucinated flags, no invented APIs, no outdated v3 patterns mislabeled as v4.

verified_claims.claim: Install Tailwind v4 with Vite using: npm install tailwindcss @tailwindcss/vite
verified_claims.evidence: Matches the official Tailwind CSS v4 Vite installation guide at tailwindcss.com exactly. The @tailwindcss/vite package and the install command are confirmed.

verified_claims.claim: Single @import "tailwindcss" replaces all three @tailwind base/components/utilities directives
verified_claims.evidence: Confirmed by official v4 docs and the v4.0 release blog. The CSS-first import is the documented replacement for the three-directive pattern.

verified_claims.claim: @source not "../legacy" syntax excludes paths from content scanning
verified_claims.evidence: Confirmed in the official 'Detecting classes in source files' documentation page at tailwindcss.com/docs/detecting-classes-in-source-files.

verified_claims.claim: bg-linear-to-* replaces bg-gradient-to-*; bg-radial and bg-conic are new gradient types
verified_claims.evidence: Confirmed by the v4.0 release blog and upgrade guide at tailwindcss.com. The rename is part of the documented breaking changes and the new gradient types are official v4 additions.

verified_claims.claim: Container queries are built into v4 core (no plugin needed), using @container class and @container/name for named containers
verified_claims.evidence: Confirmed by the v4.0 release blog: 'container queries have been added directly to core'. Previously required @tailwindcss/container-queries plugin in v3.2. Named container syntax also confirmed.

verified_claims.claim: @custom-variant uses @slot to mark where utility styles are injected
verified_claims.evidence: Confirmed in official 'Adding custom styles' docs at tailwindcss.com/docs/adding-custom-styles. The @slot placeholder and shorthand syntax shown in the cheatsheet both match the documented API.

verified_claims.claim: npx @tailwindcss/upgrade automates the v3 → v4 migration
verified_claims.evidence: Confirmed by the official upgrade guide at tailwindcss.com/docs/upgrade-guide. The tool name, command, and description of what it handles all match.

verified_claims.claim: Performance: full builds up to 10x faster, incremental builds up to 100x faster
verified_claims.evidence: Official benchmarks corroborate: full rebuilds 3.5–10x faster, incremental rebuilds >100x faster (some sources cite 182x). The cheatsheet's figures are within the documented range and are not exaggerated.
